claims.text: A hybrid MLIP and Einstein-crystal thermodynamic-integration framework can accurately predict melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed framework can accurately predict entropy of fusion for high-entropy alloys.
The proposed framework can accurately predict heat capacity for high-entropy alloys.
Direct ab initio molecular dynamics is computationally intractable for screening vast multicomponent compositional spaces.
The target materials are disordered multicomponent solid solutions with high melting points and sparse experimental data.
The MLIP will be trained on a curated set of quantum-mechanical calculations.
Thermodynamic integration using an Einstein-crystal reference state will be used to compute solid-liquid coexistence properties.
The intended domain includes alloys containing at least five principal elements at temperatures approaching or exceeding 2000 K.
An MLIP can act as a surrogate for the quantum-mechanical energy landscape.
Using an MLIP enables the long-timescale molecular dynamics needed to detect phase transitions.
AIMD is too slow to sample rare melting events in large, compositionally complex systems.
Classical empirical potentials lack sufficient transferability for multicomponent disordered alloys.
MLIPs can capture complex many-body interactions with near-DFT accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost.
The Einstein-crystal method can rigorously calculate absolute free energies for both solid and liquid phases and thereby locate the melting point.
The methodology will predict benchmark HEA melting temperatures within 5% of experimental values.
The methodology will provide reliable melting-property predictions for unexplored compositions.
Predicted entropy of fusion and heat capacity values will be consistent with the third law of thermodynamics.
The method is valid for substitutional solid solutions.
The method may fail when strong chemical ordering, intermetallic formation, or extreme magnetic effects are absent from the training data.
Transferring MLIP performance from binary and ternary systems to quinary and higher-order systems has uncertain transferability.
